A Priori Monte Carlo Simulation for Sample Size Planning for SEM Targeted Effects

Source: R/ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.Rd

Conduct a priori Monte Carlo simulation to empirically study the effects of (mis)specifications of input information on the calculated sample size. Random data are generated from the true covariance matrix but fit to the proposed model, whereas sample size is calculated based on the input covariance matrix and proposed model.

Usage

ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity(
  model,
  supposed_cov_matrix,
  true_cov_matrix = supposed_cov_matrix,
  which_path,
  width,
  specified_N = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  G = 100,
  filename = NULL,
  ...,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A single character string giving the free analysis model in lavaan model syntax (see model.syntax), the model that would be fit to the data. The target path must carry a parameter label so it can be referred to by name, for example "f2 ~ b*f1" labels the structural path b. The model may or may not be the true data generating model

supposed_cov_matrix

the population covariance matrix supposed when the sample size is planned (passed to ss_aipe_sem_path as its true_cov_matrix). It is a planning assumption, not a matrix estimated from data, and it may or may not be the true covariance matrix. The row names and column names of supposed_cov_matrix should be the same as the observed variables in model

true_cov_matrix

the true population covariance matrix, which will be used to generate random data for the simulation study. The row names and column names of true_cov_matrix should be the same as the observed variables in model. Defaults to supposed_cov_matrix

which_path

the parameter label of the targeted path, given as a character string, for example "b" for the path labeled f2 ~ b*f1 in model

width

desired confidence interval width for the model parameter of interest

specified_N

the total sample size N of each set of random data. If it is NULL, it is the sample size ss_aipe_sem_path plans from supposed_cov_matrix

conf_level

confidence level (i.e., 1- Type I error rate)

assurance

the assurance that the confidence interval obtained in a particular study will be no wider than desired (must be NULL or a value between 0.50 and 1)

G

number of replications in the Monte Carlo simulation

filename

an optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the estimate of the targeted path, its standard error, the two confidence limits, and the interval width): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv")

...

further arguments passed to sem for every fit: the planning fit to supposed_cov_matrix (through ss_aipe_sem_path), the fit to true_cov_matrix, and the fit to each simulated sample (for example std.lv = TRUE). Every name given here must be an argument or an option of lavaan (see lavOptions); any other name, and any argument without a name, is refused before a model is fitted, with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid that gives the name as it was typed

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value summarizing the a priori Monte Carlo study. The term entries are: "mean_path", "median_path", "sd_path" (summaries of the realized estimates of the targeted path across the converged replications); "mean_ci_width", "median_ci_width", "sd_ci_width" (summaries of the realized interval widths); "pct_ci_less_width" (proportion of realized widths at or below width); "pct_ci_miss_low" and "pct_ci_miss_high" (tail-specific empirical non-coverage of the population path); "total_type_I_error" (overall empirical non-coverage, the sum of the two tails); and the echoes "total_N" (the N evaluated), "true_path" (the population value of the targeted path under true_cov_matrix), "width", "conf_level", and "assurance" (present only when an assurance was supplied). The proportion rows are on the 0 to 1 scale, not percentages. The number of replications that gave an interval is attr(x, "simulation")$returned, and the number of data sets drawn again is attr(x, "simulation")$n_redrawn (see the sections below).

Details

This function implements the sample size planning methods proposed in Lai and Kelley (2011). It calls ss_aipe_sem_path to plan the sample size and to identify the targeted path, then fits the analysis model to data simulated from true_cov_matrix with sem. The analysis model is written in lavaan model syntax with the targeted path given a parameter label; see model.syntax for the syntax and sem for the fitting machinery. The population covariance matrices are most naturally produced by cov_sem from a fully fixed population model. This function requires lavaan and MASS to be installed.

Note

Occasionally a replication fails to converge when the analysis model is fit to a simulated data set. Such replications are not counted toward the G converged replications; the simulation draws fresh data and continues. A replication whose likelihood has no maximum, an error variance running off below zero while the likelihood is flat or still rising (see fa_bifactor), is treated the same way, and an analysis model with no maximum at supposed_cov_matrix or true_cov_matrix stops the function, before any replication is drawn, with an error of class dmar_no_maximum that prints the lavaan code of that fit. A safety cap stops the loop after 20 * G attempts, and a single warning is issued if fewer than G replications converged.

Replications drawn again

A simulated data set whose model fit does not converge, or whose estimate is not a maximum of the likelihood, is replaced by a new one, so such a data set is not among the replications without an interval and is in no summary row. At most 20 * G data sets are drawn in all; if that many do not give G converged fits, the function warns and summarizes the fits it has. The number of data sets drawn and set aside is the element n_redrawn of the simulation attribute, an integer read with attr(x, "simulation")$n_redrawn: 0 when every fit converged, and the total number of data sets drawn is n_redrawn plus the number of converged fits. The other elements of the record keep their meaning: attempted is G, returned the replications with an interval, and failed those without one (a converged fit whose variance for the path was negative or missing, or a replication never obtained). A large n_redrawn beside G says the model is hard to fit at this sample size, and the summaries then describe only the samples in which it could be fitted.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Lai, K., & Kelley, K. (2011). Accuracy in parameter estimation for targeted effects in structural equation modeling: Sample size planning for narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 16(2), 127–148. doi:10.1037/a0021764

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge.

Rosseel, Y. (2012). lavaan: An R package for structural equation modeling. Journal of Statistical Software, 48(2), 1–36. doi:10.18637/jss.v048.i02

See also

sem, cov_sem, ss_aipe_sem_path

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# The planning values a researcher would bring to ss_aipe_sem_path(): two
# factors, each measured by three indicators, joined by a structural path
# of 0.5, with every residual variance at 0.5.
planning_model <- "
  f1 =~ 1*y1 + 0.8*y2 + 0.8*y3
  f2 =~ 1*y4 + 0.8*y5 + 0.8*y6
  f2 ~ 0.5*f1
  f1 ~~ 1*f1
  f2 ~~ 0.75*f2
  y1 ~~ 0.5*y1; y2 ~~ 0.5*y2; y3 ~~ 0.5*y3
  y4 ~~ 0.5*y4; y5 ~~ 0.5*y5; y6 ~~ 0.5*y6
"

# The population the study will actually sample from: the same structural
# path, but noisier indicators than the planning values assumed, with
# every residual variance at 0.8.
true_model <- "
  f1 =~ 1*y1 + 0.8*y2 + 0.8*y3
  f2 =~ 1*y4 + 0.8*y5 + 0.8*y6
  f2 ~ 0.5*f1
  f1 ~~ 1*f1
  f2 ~~ 0.75*f2
  y1 ~~ 0.8*y1; y2 ~~ 0.8*y2; y3 ~~ 0.8*y3
  y4 ~~ 0.8*y4; y5 ~~ 0.8*y5; y6 ~~ 0.8*y6
"

# The free analysis model, with the targeted path labeled "b".
analysis_model <- "
  f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3
  f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6
  f2 ~ b*f1
"

supposed_cov_matrix <- cov_sem(planning_model)$sigma_theta
true_cov_matrix <- cov_sem(true_model)$sigma_theta

# The sample size planned from the optimistic measurement quality is
# evaluated against the population that actually holds. Notice that the
# mean realized width (mean_ci_width) exceeds the desired 0.30, and that
# pct_ci_less_width, the proportion of intervals no wider than desired, falls
# well below the one half that the planned sample size would deliver if
# the planning values were right. G = 10 keeps the example quick; a
# reported sensitivity study deserves the default G = 100 or more.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity(model = analysis_model,
                             supposed_cov_matrix = supposed_cov_matrix,
                             true_cov_matrix = true_cov_matrix,
                             which_path = "b", width = 0.30, G = 10)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_path          0.497
#>  median_path        0.502
#>  sd_path            0.053
#>  mean_ci_width      0.334
#>  median_ci_width    0.338
#>  sd_ci_width        0.032
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.200
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.000
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.000
#>  total_type_I_error 0.000
#>  total_N            264  
#>  true_path          0.500
#>  width              0.300
#>  conf_level         0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 10
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
